requirements.notes:
Four differentiated ideas beyond the literal ask, all shipped rather than sketched.

(1) THE COST-ROUTED CASCADE. Haiku extracts every label; a deterministic TypeScript router decides; Sonnet only ever sees an explicit escalation. It is enforced in code, not just described, and the escalation is asynchronous so the agent still gets an answer inside the latency budget.

(2) DUAL-CHANNEL WARNING RECONCILIATION. Two independent readers (VLM transcription and OCR) are reconciled by an explicit decision table whose governing rule is that the system never accuses on a single channel — a single-channel deviation returns REVIEW, never FAIL. That is a real compliance-design idea, not a feature.

(3) CONFIDENCE-TRIAGED HUMAN REVIEW QUEUE. Persisted queue with reason codes and human disposition, its own UI, and E2E coverage. This is the one docs/PRD.md labels with the word 'differentiator' outright.
